podcast.body: Brainstormed after watching Stanley Kubrick's "2001: A Space Odyssey," this song tells the story of Major Tom, an isolated astronaut. It captured the 1969 zeitgeist, was rushed by Mercury Records for the Apollo 11 moon landing, and became a UK number five hit. In 1973, it belatedly became Bowie's first US Top 40 hit, peaking at number 15/16 on the Hot 100, years after its initial release. "He called the song Space Odyssey and it would change everything, ushering Bowie into his next phase."

podcast.body: Emerging after Bowie saw Stanley Kubrick's "2001: Space Odyssey" while stoned in 1968, this song was inspired by the film's character David Bowman and possibly Tom Major, a failed British trapeze artist who also made garden gnomes. Initially rejected multiple times as a "novelty song," it became Bowie's first hit due to the BBC using it as a theme for their Apollo Moon mission coverage. It reached number five on the UK charts, but only peaked at number 124 in North America initially, before a 1973 re-release saw it reach number 15 in the US and number 16 in Canada. "That song became David Bowie's first ever hit. And only because of some lucky timing."

podcast.body: The original studio recording of "Space Oddity" in 1969 was a psychedelic folk rocker about Major Tom, which Bowie re-recorded later that year after signing a new record deal. It debuted in Billboard in August 1969 and bubbled under the Hot 100, peaking at number 124. In early 1973, four years after its recording, RCA Records re-issued the song on 45, pushing it to American Top 40 radio with new Ziggy Stardust imagery. It finally made the Hot 100, peaking at number 15, solidifying Bowie's alien persona and defining him in the public imagination. "In early 1973, four years after it had been recorded, Space Audity finally made the Hot 100, peaking at number 15."

podcast.body: This dark, pseudo-folk song was written by Bowie in the context of a painful breakup with Hermione Farthingdale, feelings of depression, and a fascination with the American space program, particularly the Apollo moon landing and the film *2001, A Space Odyssey*. The very first version was recorded on February 2nd, 1969, the day after his breakup. Several more versions followed, with the definitive one recorded on June 20th and released on July 11th, just in time for the Apollo 11 mission. Broadcasters, including the BBC, adopted it as an unofficial theme for the July 20th moon landing. The song became Bowie's breakthrough hit and turned him into a star, though he feared becoming a one-hit wonder. Its lyrics about Major Tom sparked speculation about the character's identity. Bowie recorded the definitive version after a chance meeting with Elton John led him to a producer. "The definitive version was recorded June 20th, and then released to the public on July 11th, just in time for the Apollo 11 mission."
